text: For a spatially flat FLRW universe dominated by pressureless matter (w = 0), integrating the Friedmann equations gives a scale factor that grows as:
explanation: Matter dilutes as ρ_m ∝ a⁻³, and the flat Friedmann equation then yields a(t) ∝ t^(2/3). Radiation (ρ_r ∝ a⁻⁴) instead gives a ∝ t^(1/2), a cosmological constant gives exponential de Sitter growth a ∝ e^(Ht), and a curvature-dominated universe gives a ∝ t. Swapping the matter (t^(2/3)) and radiation (t^(1/2)) scalings is the common error the table in Section 47.2 is designed to prevent.
